featuredImages.title: Webb's First Deep Field
featuredImages.description: The deepest and sharpest infrared image of the distant universe to date, showing galaxy cluster SMACS 0723 as it appeared 4.6 billion years ago

featuredImages.title: Pillars of Creation
featuredImages.description: Iconic image of star-forming region in the Eagle Nebula, 6,500 light-years away. These towering structures are columns of cool interstellar hydrogen gas and dust

featuredImages.title: Cosmic Cliffs in the Carina Nebula
featuredImages.description: Stellar nursery NGC 3324 in the Carina Nebula, revealing previously invisible areas of star birth captured in infrared light

featuredImages.title: Perseverance Rover on Mars
featuredImages.description: Perseverance rover exploring Jezero Crater, searching for signs of ancient microbial life and collecting rock samples for future return to Earth

featuredImages.title: Jupiter's Swirling Clouds
featuredImages.description: Juno spacecraft captures stunning details of Jupiter's turbulent atmosphere, including the Great Red Spot and swirling storms

featuredImages.title: Saturn's Majestic Rings
featuredImages.description: Cassini's 13-year mission revealed Saturn's rings in unprecedented detail, along with discoveries on moons like Enceladus and Titan

featuredImages.title: Andromeda Galaxy
featuredImages.description: Our nearest large galactic neighbor, M31, containing one trillion stars. Located 2.5 million light-years away and on a collision course with the Milky Way

featuredImages.title: Earth from Space
featuredImages.description: Our home planet as seen from the International Space Station and Earth observation satellites, showing continents, oceans, and atmospheric phenomena

featuredImages.title: First Image of a Black Hole
featuredImages.description: First direct visual evidence of a supermassive black hole at the center of galaxy M87, 55 million light-years away

featuredImages.title: Blue Marble - Earth from Apollo 17
featuredImages.description: One of the most iconic images of Earth taken by Apollo 17 crew, showing Africa, Antarctica, and the Arabian Peninsula

featuredImages.title: Apollo Moon Surface
featuredImages.description: Astronauts on the lunar surface during Apollo missions, showing the desolate beauty of Earth's only natural satellite

featuredImages.title: Orion Nebula
featuredImages.description: One of the brightest nebulae visible to the naked eye, located 1,344 light-years away. A stellar nursery where new stars are being born

featuredImages.title: Crab Nebula Supernova Remnant
featuredImages.description: Remains of a supernova explosion observed by Chinese astronomers in 1054 AD, powered by a rapidly spinning neutron star at its center

featuredImages.title: Spiral Galaxy NGC 1300
featuredImages.description: A barred spiral galaxy 61 million light-years away, showing elegant spiral arms and a prominent central bar structure

featuredImages.title: Hubble Ultra Deep Field
featuredImages.description: One of the deepest images of the universe ever taken, showing nearly 10,000 galaxies in a tiny patch of sky
